title: A verbatim tag that is neither local nor a URI
notes: Production 98 matches `!<$:?>`, because every character is a URI character, but section 6.9.1 requires a verbatim tag to begin with `!` or to be a valid URI, and `$:?` is not one (a URI starts with a scheme: a letter). Example 6.25 lists `- !<$:?> bar` as invalid. The prefix `- !<` can still become valid, because `!<!x>` is a local tag, but no URI begins with `$` (RFC 3986 section 3: a scheme starts with a letter), so the first character that cannot belong to any valid document is the `$`, at column 5. Compare diagnostics/verbatim-tag-of-a-lone-bang-is-invalid.

provenance.reference: Found while reading the source of a library whose tag scanner accepted any run of URI characters in a verbatim tag.
